source: វិទ្យាការទប់ស្កាត់ និងកម្ចាត់សមាសភាពបទព្រុងលើដំណាំទុរេន (Prevention and Control of Harmful Organisms on Durian), Cambodian technical extension document compiled with reference to CABI Crop Protection Compendium and durian pest/disease literature, 28pp
text: Mealybug (Planococcus lilacinus) is a small, soft-bodied, white waxy-coated insect that clusters on young shoots, flower clusters, and the surface of developing fruit, feeding by sucking plant sap. Heavy infestations weaken new growth and can cause flower and young fruit drop; mealybugs also excrete honeydew that promotes black sooty mould growth on leaves and fruit surfaces, further reducing the fruit's marketability. Ants are often found tending mealybug colonies (protecting them from natural predators in exchange for the honeydew), so ant activity on flower clusters or fruit is a useful early warning sign to check for mealybugs. General control approach: prune out and destroy heavily infested shoots, encourage natural predators, and treat with an appropriate insecticide when infestation is heavy, following label instructions; this source's scanned pages did not consistently show legible product names or exact dosage rates, so growers should confirm a specific product and rate with a local agricultural supplier or extension officer rather than relying on a dosage transcribed from this pass.
